<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f4b1f9ee0865544d0a404a2ceb0b02b4d77cb69c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6e84da946833cbf35fcff6cf94e0aeb5e32d5ad6` — the merge of head `5e9d2802a6cb2c07c1cda4a707e4fef82afdf3bb` into base `f4b1f9ee0865544d0a404a2ceb0b02b4d77cb69c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6e84da946833cbf35fcff6cf94e0aeb5e32d5ad6 && git checkout 6e84da946833cbf35fcff6cf94e0aeb5e32d5ad6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f4b1f9ee0865544d0a404a2ceb0b02b4d77cb69c 5e9d2802a6cb2c07c1cda4a707e4fef82afdf3bb && git checkout -B drift-repro f4b1f9ee0865544d0a404a2ceb0b02b4d77cb69c && git merge --no-ff 5e9d2802a6cb2c07c1cda4a707e4fef82afdf3bb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f4b1f9ee0865544d0a404a2ceb0b02b4d77cb69c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Prose face (`.changeset/31470-cbp-omitted-required-raw-parse-door.md`) checked sentence by sentence for the seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

The dev's open question (do the save doors really read the omission as optional?) was MEASURED, not taken from the ruling record.

**Save door trace (true on head).** The object save door is `saveMetaItem` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts`); its spec gate at :1424-1429 runs `resolveOverlaySchema(...)` → `schema.safeParse(request.item)`, and `resolveOverlaySchema` (`protocol-meta-type-schema.ts:556-562`) returns `ObjectSchema` (`kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts:93`) — the raw parse, not `create()`. The only conversion replays in that file are the flow one (:1316) and stored-row `convertStoredItemDetailed` (:2507); no `request.item` rewrite before the gate touches `required`. The D2 conversion `cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted` is `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, and `applyConversions` skips retired entries unless `includeRetired` (`conversions/apply.ts:159`), which only stored-row rehydration pins (`apply.ts:44-47`, `protocol-stored-item-conversion.ts:93`). The registry write-through registers the body as written and validates with `ObjectSchema.parse` (`objectql/src/registry.ts:7728, 7912`). Studio reaches the same door (`rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts:364`). So "a save door reads an omitted `required` as the optional master" is true of the code. Once stored, read-back replays the retired conversion and the row reads `required: true` — consistent with the entry's "keeps meaning required … on stored rows".

Sentence by sentence:
- Entry header comment (`18.cbp-optional-master-admitted.ts:14-19`): true (trace above; `defineStack` pinned by the new test and `conversions/cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted.test.ts:117`); the ruling citation matches record 6687830530 verbatim.
- `replacement` (:44-48): true; "`os lint` reports the omission at `error`" true (`lint/src/data-model-rules.ts:417-418, 447-448`, pinned at `data-model-rules.master-detail-required.test.ts:110`).
- `acceptanceCriteria` (:70-72): true (probe + trace).
- Docblock (`controlled-by-parent-master.ts:160-166`): true; builder force `forceCbpMasterDetailRequired` at `object.zod.ts:4509`, applied :4679; "Reads `required` as written" kept (:170).
- Order item 4 (report only): the D2 docblock is already fixed on main by `f1206610a` (#31055). Nothing owed.
- **nit**: the `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment for `cbp-optional-master-admitted` (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template:1322-1335`) still names only the builder's reading. True as far as it goes, outside the order's two named texts.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` — correct: only a JSDoc and string-literal content of a `SemanticMigration` entry change. `Metadata-protocol: none` — correct. A patch changeset (not `skip-changeset`) is right: the entry ships — `gen:migration-registry` (`scripts/build-migration-registry.ts:145`) → `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR` (`src/migrations/index.ts:26-32`) → the `./migrations` export; `os migrate meta` prints `judge.replacement` (`cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:841,851`); the upgrade guide renders the same fields (`spec/scripts/build-upgrade-guide.ts:153-155`).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Four files, all inside the order's surface. No behaviour change: the non-test product hunks are comment text and string-literal content only. The merge commit `5e9d2802a6` brings only `docs/adr/0143-…` from `origin/main`.
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note.

### ④ Design judgment

- The added clauses hold against the cited code and the acceptance scenario (safeParse / defineStack / save door admit; `create()` forces; stored rows convert). Ruling cited by record id.
- Test (`controlled-by-parent-master.test.ts:140-165`): the field omits `required`; each door has its own assertions (`create()` → `true` / `optional:false`; `safeParse` → `false` / `optional:true`; `defineStack` → `false` / `optional:true`), so a change to any one door trips a distinct `expect`. Cites ruling A / 6687830530 / #31470. The body's claim that no earlier test pinned all three in one place checks out.
- **nit**: `defineStack` casts (`as never`, `as unknown as {…}`) in the test; no effect on what is asserted.
